title: What a portfolio is for: evidence, not a museum

videos.script: A portfolio is not a collection. It is evidence, put where the person deciding about you will look for it. {{evidence}} That person has a question. Can you do the job? Your CV answers it with claims: Python, Docker, SQL. A portfolio answers it with something they can open. {{claims}} And they will not open everything. They open one thing, and they judge you by the thing they happened to open. So twenty repositories are not twenty chances. They are twenty ways to be judged by the weakest one. {{museum}} This course builds one project, and builds it to the end: chosen, cut down, finished, deployed, explained. Every lesson adds one piece to it, and every lesson shows the same piece on a real example, a small service called loanbook. {{course}} This first lesson is about who reads a portfolio, and what they are looking for when they do.
